newsitem.title: CHINA: Guangdong Industrial buys New Asia Fast Food stake.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Industrial buys New Asia Fast Food stake.

text.p: Guangdong Industrial (Group), parent company of Guangdong Investment, has spent 55.925 million yuan to buy a 41.8 percent stake in Shanghai New Asia Fast Food, officials said on Wednesday.

Guangdong Industrial bought 22.37 million legal person shares in New Asia Fast Food at 2.5 yuan each, of which 12.08 million shares were from Shanghai New Asia (Group) Co and 10.29 million shares from Shanghai Erfangji Co, officials said.
"We sold Guangdong Industrial the shares at 2.5 yuan each against the cost of one yuan each," Erfangji and New Asia (Group) officials told Reuters.
Guangdong Industrial will put capital into New Asia Fast Food to upgrade the firm's technology, a Guangdong Industrial official said.

Guangdong Industrial, which has three listed companies including Guangdong Investment and Guangnan Holding, wants to have listings on mainland China markets as well, he said but declined to give further details.
New Asia (Group) still holds 267 million shares or 4.99 percent of Fast Food, but Erfangji sold its entire holding.
New Asia Fast Food has had a poor results record over the past year, which was why New Asia (Group) and Erfangji wanted to sell, company officials said.
"Fast Food will post earning per share of less than 0.01 yuan for 1996 because of serious competition in Shanghai's fast food market," an New Asia (Group) official said.

In the first half of 1996, Fast Food posted net profits of 449,175 yuan, down sharply from 2.915 million yuan in the same 1995 period and earnings per share were 0.0084 yuan compared with 0.0545 yuan for the first half of 1995.
Fast Food posted net profits of 5.17 million yuan in 1995, little changed from 5.14 million yuan in 1994.
